title: Conscience as Capital: The Economic Case for Moral Density in Market Systems
abstract: This paper argues that conscience — the internal faculty of moral self-evaluation — is an unrecognized form of capital. Like physical capital (machinery) and human capital (skills), conscience generates productive capacity. Unlike these forms, its output is not measured by conventional economics. This paper proposes a framework for understanding conscience as capital, drawing on Hiroi Chikuro's morality science, the author's V=N/D value density theory, and the Hikari Currency implementation as a working prototype.

title: The Ki-Net Synchronization Model of Cardiac Rhythm: A Boundary-Surface Theory of Heart Function
abstract: Contemporary cardiology understands cardiac rhythm as an electrical signaling system: the sinoatrial node generates an impulse, which propagates through conduction pathways to trigger synchronized muscle contraction. title: Quasi-Periodic Oscillations in C3 ISP Blazars: Evidence from Fermi-LAT FAVA 17-Year Light Curves
abstract: We present a Lomb-Scargle periodicity analysis of five Intermediate-frequency Peaked BL Lac objects (ISP blazars) belonging to the C3 clustering group, using 17 years (2008–2025) of weekly Fermi-LAT Flare Advocate and Variability Analysis (FAVA) σ-excess light curves. title: Complete X-Ray Spectral Classification of ISP Blazars in the 4LAC-DR3 High-Variability Sample: A Ten-Source Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Study and the Class-S/H Neutrino Prediction Framework
abstract: We present the complete X-ray spectral classification of all 10 intermediate synchrotron-peaked (ISP) BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high-variability blazar sample, using Swift-XRT hardness ratio (HR) analysis. Across 214,715 total photons from archival PC-mode observations spanning 2005–2023, we classify each source as either Class-H (spectral hardening at high flux: β > 0) or Class-S (spectral softening at high flux: β < 0). The result is unambiguous: **9 of 10 sources are Class-S; the sole Class-H source is TXS 0506+056** — the only blazar with a confirmed astrophysical neutrino association (IceCube-170922A). title: Biorhythm-Moon Phase Correlation with IceCube GOLD Events: A Predictive Window Analysis
abstract: This study investigates whether the biorhythm cycles of the researcher (birth date: August 12, 1970) and lunar phase correlate with the timing of IceCube GOLD-class neutrino alerts. Analysis of 62 GOLD events (2019–2026) reveals a statistically anomalous inverse correlation: 69.4% of GOLD events occurred during biorhythm composite negative phases (vs. 50% random expectation), and 38.7% coincided with new or full moon phases (vs. ~10.2% random expectation). The combined condition (composite negative × new/full moon) yielded 29.0% of GOLD occurrences against a 5.1% random baseline — approximately 6× above chance. These findings suggest a predictive window framework for anticipating GOLD-class neutrino events.
keywords: biorhythm, chronobiology, cardiac rhythm, living laboratory, social experiment, TheYKHC, Yoshimitsu Katayama, ORCID:0009-0006-2290-6593

title: X-ray Spectral Softening in AO 0235+164: Swift-XRT Analysis and Class-S Classification
abstract: We present a systematic X-ray spectral variability analysis of the intermediate-frequency-peaked BL Lac object (ISP BL Lac) AO 0235+164 using archival Swift X-ray Telescope (XRT) data spanning 2007–2024. From 180 valid observations totaling 63,028 photons, we compute the hardness ratio (HR = (H−S)/(H+S), where S: 0.3–1.2 keV, H: 1.2–10 keV) as a function of X-ray count rate. We find a statistically significant negative correlation (β = −0.682, r = −0.434, p = 1.14 × 10⁻⁹), indicating spectral softening with increasing brightness. This behavior classifies AO 0235+164 as **Class-S** within the Class-S/H framework established for ISP BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high sample. title: A Systematic Overview of 550 Cross-Domain Hypotheses: Structure, Generative Core, and Thematic Distribution (2010–2026)
abstract: This paper provides a systematic overview of approximately 550 hypotheses generated by the author over the period 2010–2026, spanning astrophysics, theoretical physics, economics, linguistics, medicine, and civilizational design. title: The Ground-Cosmic Independence Test: Are Macro Conditions and KOKU Statistically Independent?
abstract: This paper tests whether the Ground Score (macro) and Cosmic Score (KOKU) components of the Tendo Economics Two-Layer Framework are statistically independent. Using the complete IceCube GOLD-event dataset (N=53, 2019-2025), three correlations are computed: KOKU × gold price (Ground Score proxy) r=+0.060 (near-zero — independence confirmed); KOKU × 7-day return r=-0.101 (weak negative — the central anomaly); gold price × return r=+0.232 (weak positive — regime effect). The 60/40 weighting scheme is empirically justified by near-zero KOKU-ground correlation. The unexpected finding is that KOKU-return correlation is weakly negative across all price regimes, contradicting the simple accumulation hypothesis. title: KOKU Interval Analysis: Complete Historical Dataset 2019–2026 — Statistical Structure of IceCube GOLD-Event Silence Intervals and Gold Market Co-Movement
abstract: Complete statistical analysis of KOKU intervals (N=54) derived from the IceCube GOLD-event dataset (June 2019–December 2025, N=55 events). Key findings: Mean KOKU=43.8 days, SD=47.0, right-skewed distribution. Weak positive KOKU-signalness correlation (r=+0.127). KOKU-stratified 7-day gold returns reveal a non-monotonic pattern: 0-30d (+2.19%), 31-60d (+0.49%), 61-100d (+1.93%), >100d (+1.70%). The 31-60 day dip is identified as the primary unresolved anomaly. Current KOKU=164 days (z=+2.56σ, P=2.4% under Poisson null, 1-in-42 event). Historical comparators at KOKU 182-188 days produced +1.83% and +2.09% returns. Pre-registered central estimate for CSS Event Window (May 25-30, 2026): +1.5% to +2.1% (7-day window). Explicit limitations: N too small for definitive conclusions; 7-day window differs from established 72h finding; gold price regime confounding.
